# Phase 10 — Reproduction and research release audit

**Status: BLOCKED / NOT PASSED.** The repository rebuilt and all available software tests passed from a new Release build directory. The committed partial Phase 9 summary was regenerated byte-for-byte from the committed 19-row JSONL, and its hashes and freeze metadata match. This reproduces the **derived summary**, not the original benchmark solver attempts; those attempts were intentionally not rerun, and no independent researcher has repeated them.

## What reproduced

A clean CMake Release build with GCC 13.3.0, CMake 3.28.3, Python 3.12.3, and GMP 6.3.0 passed all **11/11 CTest targets**. The Phase 9 Python harness tests passed **13/13**. Using the exact frozen XAI and Ganak binaries, the synthetic stress suite passed **11/11** again; its compact outcome record is [`Phase-10-stress-rerun.json`](Phase-10-stress-rerun.json). These are build and software-fixture results, not new benchmark outcomes.

The Phase 10 harness regenerated `RESULT/Phase-9-public-even-partial-summary-v2.json` from `RESULT/Phase-9-public-even.jsonl`; the bytes matched exactly. It verified all row-level stdout/stderr hashes, checked the fixed 19 indices (0–36, even only), recomputed all 95 attempt statuses, and confirmed the report still says `evaluation_complete: false` and `phase9_practical_gate: false`. The original freeze manifest’s **39 locked source files** match commit `a1a65b5ffdeab261bcdeaf7151c03b0c66213403`. The archive and both frozen solver executables also match their manifest hashes at the recorded local paths.

## What the partial benchmark actually shows

The recorded diagnostic covers **19/98** eligible public-even records. Ganak returned exact counts on 10/19. XAI full and each of its three ablations returned **0/19**; none of the XAI configurations completed jointly with Ganak. There were no observed count mismatches among the attempted cases, but zero directly verified XAI counts and no estimable exact-match fraction. The independent exhaustive oracle was eligible for 0/19.

| System | Exact completions | Other recorded statuses |
|---|---:|---|
| Ganak | 10/19 | 6 memory limits; 3 timeouts |
| XAI full | 0/19 | 11 resource limits; 6 timeouts; 2 memory limits |
| XAI without unit propagation | 0/19 | 12 resource limits; 4 timeouts; 3 memory limits |
| XAI without components | 0/19 | 13 resource limits; 4 timeouts; 2 memory limits |
| XAI first-branch ablation | 0/19 | 11 resource limits; 7 timeouts; 1 memory limit |

Across all 95 attempts there were 10 exact completions, 47 resource-limit outcomes, 24 timeouts, and 14 memory-limit outcomes. Three attempts exceeded even 602 seconds of measured wall time, against the 600-second per-process wall limit: index 0 XAI first-branch (766,131 ms), index 0 XAI full (624,606 ms), and index 4 Ganak (814,576 ms). These remain disclosed as deviations; none was repeated or converted into a valid result.

The leakage audit opened odd-indexed formula bodies for its predeclared checks. It found two near-duplicate odd records, indices 173 and 177, related to public index 176; after those exclusions the audited final-odd claim set contains 95 eligible records. **No final-odd record was solver-scored or used for tuning.**

## Claims and release limits

The README, project overview, roadmap, test notes, specifications, and phase reports were checked against the artifacts. Stale repository inventories were updated to include Phases 8–10; the README now describes the 19/98 diagnostic and its zero XAI completions; the roadmap distinguishes the synthetic in-process orchestrator from a production runtime; and the orchestration and learning specifications clarify that the later leakage audit inspected odd formulas without scoring them. The public description now limits test claims to fixtures, limits benchmark statements to the reduced diagnostic, and makes no claim of general intelligence, novelty, benchmark superiority, production readiness, proof verification, or real-world safety.

The frozen protocol, archive snapshot, binary hashes, run records, and synthetic stress artifact are available locally and identified by hashes, but the archive and solver binaries are not stored in the Git repository. The JSONL preserves outputs and resource measurements, not the original decompressed formula bodies. A clean clone therefore needs the specified data and exact frozen binaries to run this verification harness; the report does not claim that a new researcher reproduced the original solver outcomes.

## Open issues and recommendation

Phase 9 remains incomplete: 79 public-even records were not scored, the final-odd set was not solver-scored, XAI produced no exact count in the observed prefix, the independent oracle applied to none of those records, and resource-control overruns were observed. No calibration, predictive score, conformal coverage, or selective-risk estimate is available for this unlabeled counting archive. The implementation also lacks a production exact-WMC proof verifier and authenticated provenance; the Phase 8 verifier and broader orchestration tests are synthetic fixtures.

**Recommendation: narrow.** Keep the repository as a research-software artifact, but limit empirical claims to the recorded 19-case diagnostic and synthetic software fixtures. Do not claim benchmark competence or practical XAI solver performance. Any further benchmark evaluation should use the frozen options without tuning on observed outcomes, retain input hashes and complete run outputs, enforce the declared stop limits, and be independently reproduced before a release gate is reconsidered. Any production or high-impact deployment remains a separate proposal requiring its own review.

**Phase 10 gate: BLOCKED / NOT PASSED.** This work verifies the clean build, tests, hashes, metadata, and byte-identical summary regeneration. It does not meet the independent-reproduction requirement for the historical benchmark attempts. The Phase 10 gate is therefore not marked complete, and the Phase 9 gate remains not passed.
